units.title: Retention challenge 1
units.lesson: Retrieve the idea from memory before reading the feedback. A small recall result is evidence from these questions only.
units.question: A fictional survey finds 18 existing cases among 90 examined people. What is the snapshot prevalence?
rationales: This uses existing cases over the examined group.
units.hint: Use cases divided by examined people.

units.title: Retention challenge 2
units.lesson: Retrieve the idea from memory before reading the feedback. A small recall result is evidence from these questions only.
units.question: During follow-up, 6 new cases arise among 120 initially at-risk people. What is the cumulative incidence for that period?
rationales: This uses new cases and the initially at-risk denominator.
units.hint: New cases over initially at-risk people.
